questions.q: Which set lists the four things you supply to an Azure ML sweep job?
questions.explain: A sweep job needs a search space, a sampling method, an objective (primary metric and goal), and limits on trials and concurrency.

questions.q: A sweep job never picks the best trial. The most likely cause is that...
options: The cluster has too many nodes
The search space uses Uniform instead of Choice
The training script logs a metric under a different name than primary_metric
questions.explain: The primary metric name must exactly match the metric the script logs with mlflow.log_metric, or the service has nothing to optimize.

questions.q: Which sampling method only works with Choice (discrete) hyperparameters?
questions.explain: Grid sampling exhaustively tries every combination, so it can only be used with discrete choice values.

questions.q: What does an early termination policy such as median stopping do?
options: Cancels trials that are performing worse than the others while the sweep is running
Stops the whole sweep after the first trial
questions.explain: Early termination policies cancel poor performing trials to save compute, comparing each trial's primary metric with the others.

questions.q: Why should heavy data preparation happen outside the sweep?
options: Each trial restarts training from scratch, repeating any preparation inside it
Preparation makes the primary metric unreadable
Sweep jobs only accept CSV files
questions.explain: Every trial re-runs the training script including data loading, so repeated preparation wastes compute; a pipeline can do it once beforehand.
